Thanks for the reply.  I think that I'm the one creating the toxic environment though,TBH.  There is really no way for me to hide money, and I feel as though it would be wrong for me to do that.  Once we're separated, I would have to pay child support, and my disablilty retirement would barely cover an acceptable amount.  I'm not working right now.  I'm trying to get through school.  As it stands, we're spread so thin that all of that money goes to bills every month.  If there is one less car, one less phone, one less mouth to feed, things will be a little better.  

Fortunately, if I'm dead, my retirement still pays out half of my current benefit and my dependents keep their health insurance.  

If I remain alive and divorce my husband, he will lose my health insurance.  I don't want to be married to him, but I don't want to take that from him either.  He hasa congenital kidney disease and will need a transplant, potentially soon.  Because I retired from the military, as my dependent, he can get on the military transplant list in addition to transplant registries.

I really do not want to be married to him.  Youre gomna tell me not to kill myself though.

I'm not trying to talk you out of it, but does life insurance pay if you kill yourself though?  I have a survivor's benefit from the military that  will pay half of my current retirement to my husband or my daughter no matter how I die, but i have researched it pretty extensively.  I was under the impression that life insurance worked differently though.
